desk.headline: Q3 non-GAAP EPS up 13% to R$2.19, beat; revenue flat at R$5.09bn, miss (reported 16 Nov); US$0.26 dividend declared; no guidance
results: The queued 16 November filing announces a cash dividend of US$0.26 a share, payable on 30 December to holders on record on 14 December. PagBank's Q3 results came out the same day in a separate filing.
Total revenue and income was flat at R$5.09bn; payments revenue fell 5% as payment volume grew only 1%.
Non-GAAP net income rose 7% to R$611m (R$2.19 a share), helped by lower funding costs; GAAP net income rose 5% to R$584m.
The loan book grew 25% to R$5.2bn, led by working-capital loans, but bad loans over 90 days rose to 3.8% from 2.6% and credit-loss charges rose 47%.
Deposits rose 8% to R$42.8bn; about R$2.1bn went back to shareholders over 12 months, and a further US$150m buyback was approved in September.

guidance.summary: PagBank gives no revenue or earnings guidance. It expects a payout of about R$400m in December and at least R$2bn in distributions through 2028, and keeps an 18–22% target for its capital (BIS) ratio, now 25.2%.

watch: Whether rising bad loans slow as the unsecured loan book grows.
Payment volume and payments revenue, which were weak in Q3.
Delivery of the planned dividends and buybacks.
